headline.process: Rain-associated acoustic expansion is best explained at the ecological-process level as recurrent activation of a latent local acoustic metacommunity, not uniform amplification, weak-call detectability, stop relocation, observer turnover, or literal first appearance.
headline.chorus_transition: The site-memory x rain interaction localizes most clearly to CallingIndex 2: previously used species-site combinations are preferentially pushed from silence into overlapping-call chorus onset as rainfall contrast increases. CI1-only and CI3-only site-memory interactions are not individually supported after pair x species fixed effects.
headline.full_chorus_population_effect: Despite the CI3-specific site-memory interaction being imprecise after species control, the population-level 0-to-CI3 full-chorus rainfall association itself is robust in the full and same-observer+physical-site samples.
headline.spatial_depth: Once route-new taxa activate, the unusual spatial signal is excess third-and-later-stop participation, overwhelmingly carried by CI2-3 taxa; unusual geographic clustering conditional on occupied-stop count is not established.
headline.taxonomic_scope: Strong activation is diffuse across many taxa rather than dominated by one or a few species.
headline.geographic_scope: Aggregate NAAMP generality is strong to leave-one-state-out analyses, but state-specific effects are heterogeneous and cross-continental universality is not established.
headline.proximal_cause: The exact physiological/environmental trigger remains unresolved; coarse wetland hydroperiod/system, simple chorus facilitation, simple thermal background, survey round, and an acute one-day window do not explain the robust process.

within_pair_species_site_memory.interpretation: With pair and species fixed, prior same-site use selectively amplifies the rain response at CI2 overlapping-call onset; CI1-only and CI3-only interactions are individually imprecise.

full_chorus_raw_site_memory.boundary: These raw memory shares are composition-sensitive; pair x species fixed-effect results above are the stronger site-specific inference.

safest_ecological_conclusion: Recent rain does not simply make an existing frog chorus louder. It preferentially reactivates previously used local species-site combinations from acoustic silence into overlapping-call chorus activity, while recurrent resident taxa deepen participation across multiple sites. Full choruses also increase at the population level, but the site-memory interaction itself is most clearly localized to CI2 chorus onset after species identity is controlled. This is a behavioural/reproductive activation mechanism at the ecological-process level; the proximal hydrological or physiological trigger is not identified.
do_not_claim: All states or continents show the same effect.
Temporary wetlands are the identified mediator.
Palustrine habitat is the identified mediator.
Full CI3 chorus site-memory is independently proven after species control.
A specific hydration, endocrine, humidity or pressure pathway is identified.
analysis_pause_reason: The main mechanistic alternatives accessible with the current public NAAMP data have now been tested. Additional post hoc analyses risk diminishing interpretability; further proximal-cause resolution would require independent hydrology/microclimate or continuous acoustic data.
